newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah steady in tight range trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah steady in tight range trading.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was steady against the dollar in lifeless early trading on Thursday.
Dealers said trading remained slow, with offshore players holding on to their long forward positions and local investors shorting rupiah in the forward market.
They said volume in the cash market was thin and rates moved in a very narrow range of 50 cents.
"I hear regional players want to take a break from last month's turbulence," one European bank dealer said, referring to the Indonesian election and attacks on the Thai baht.
Spot rupiah was at 2,428.6/29.0 at 0300 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,428.5/29.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,427.85/28.30 and 2,427.6/27.9, respectively.
A Japanese bank dealer said the underlying sentiment suggested offshore players remained uncomfortable with the Thai market, driving them to extend long forward rupiah positions.
The central bank has said it has no plan to copy Thai steps to squeeze offshore players in the swap market.
The European bank dealer expected the dollar-rupiah rate to range between 2,425.0 and 2,430.0 in the short-term, with the dollar seen top heavy at the 2,430.0 level.
"We have plenty of buy orders at the 2,425.0 level. I don't think we could move closer to that level," he said, adding that further downtrend was limited by the central bank's band.
Dealers said swap rates were relatively stable on the back of a steady money market in the morning. Overnight money was hovering at around 10.5/11.5 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.3/0.4 and tom/next at 0.8/1.0.
The European bank dealer said forward rates were likely to decline if Thai authorities dismantled its two-tier market.
"I think six-month swaps could collapse to the 70 level if that happens," he said, referring to the ample rupiah market.
He said local players were now buyers of short-term swaps while offshore was selling with the positions reversed in the forward market because of the Thai factor.
Dealers said there was no immediate implication on dollar-rupiah from the volatile dollar-yen market. Indonesia has set a dollar-yen exchange rate at 110 for its 1997/98 budget.
One-month swaps were at 12.50/13.25, two at 25.0/26.0, three at 38.5/39.5 and six at 78.5/80.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,420/2,612 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,420/2,468 on Wednesday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
